title: Retroactive PII Drift Detector & Rescrub Orchestrator for Console Analytics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Context: Our analytics event schema has evolved rapidly; new fields and third-party integrations are occasionally introducing PII into events (e.g., emails in free-form 'metadata', phone numbers embedded in text blobs). Existing ingestion scrubbing catches declared PII fields at write-time, but it misses schema drift and historical events. Problem: we need a safe, auditable way to detect PII drift, run retroactive scrubs over historical partitions, and emit verifiable deletion/scrub manifests for compliance and downstream consumers without breaking analytics jobs or reintroducing PII during reprocessing. Requirements: detect candidates for PII drift, map fields to scrubbing transforms, orchestrate replay-safe rescrub/backfill with throttling, produce attestable manifests and audit logs, honor legal holds and retention windows, and integrate with existing retention-enforcer and console dashboards. Constraints: cost and I/O on backfills must be bounded, pipeline must not compromise production query latency, changes must be reversible for debugging (retain original masked hashes in ephemeral workspace), and security/compliance must approve transformation heuristics. Proposed approach: implement a PII Drift Detector that runs nightly jobs over event schema registry diffs and a lightweight sample of ingested events to surface new high-risk fields. For confirmed drift, create a rescrub plan at the partition level (by ingestion date) that is executed by a Rescrub Orchestrator. The orchestrator will: 1) produce a copy-on-write scrubbed layer in S3/warehouse for affected ranges with stable object naming and immutability, 2) write a signed scrub manifest listing affected objects, record hashes and a unique attestation token stored in the audit log index, 3) notify downstream consumers via the existing lineage topic (Kafka) so they can re-point materialized views, and 4) schedule throttled rewriting jobs using existing worker fleet with CPU/IO budgets. We'll provide a safe mode that uses redaction + reversible salted hashing for debug windows, and a final irreversible redaction mode for legal deletion. We'll also add end-to-end integration tests and a canary rescrub run on a tiny customer cohort before general rollout.
acceptance_criteria: PII Drift Detector job runs nightly and produces a ranked list of candidate fields with confidence scores and example counts
Authorized operator can create a Rescrub Plan that targets specific ingestion-date partitions and chooses scrub mode (reversible-salt | irreversible-redact)
Rescrub Orchestrator executes a plan and produces a signed scrub manifest with object paths, pre/post hashes (where reversible), and an attestation token stored in audit index
Downstream lineage topic receives a stable notification for each manifest and at least one consumer (analytics view) successfully re-points to scrubbed objects in a canary run
End-to-end integration tests validate that scrubbing removes PII examples in sample queries and that retention-enforcer honors legal hold exceptions
Performance budget: average rewrite throughput >= 30 MB/s per worker and cluster IO does not increase production query tail latency by more than 5% during backfill windows
Security & Legal sign-off recorded in ticket comments before irreversible mode is enabled
tasks: Design PII detection heuristics and schema-diff sampling approach (data science collaboration)
Implement PII Drift Detector job and integrate with schema registry and sample store
Design Rescrub Plan schema and manifest spec (signed, immutable format)
Build Rescrub Orchestrator service with scheduler, throttling, and retry semantics
Add S3/warehouse copy-on-write layer and object naming convention for scrubbed snapshots
Integrate manifest publication with lineage Kafka topic and update consumer adapters
Add audit index writes for attestations and hook into retention-enforcer to honor legal-hold flags
Create integration and canary tests; run a canary on synthetic dataset and one internal team dataset
Prepare runbooks and operator UI in Console for plan creation, monitoring, and abort
Security review and legal review for scrub heuristics and irreversible deletion flow
notes: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting — aligned with Data Privacy and Legal on scope. We must retain attestation info for 7 years per compliance.

2026-02-20: Early prototype of detector found emails in 'note' field for ~0.3% of events in last 90 days (internal test dataset). False positives using naive regex are high; need NLP-assisted heuristics.

2026-02-25: Trade-off discussion — full historical reprocessing is expensive. Decided to support partitioned rescrub with operator-controlled throttle and sampling-first canary to reduce blast radius.
2026-03-02: Storage design review — agreed to implement copy-on-write scrubbed path instead of in-place rewrite to allow fast rollback and provenance checks.

2026-03-06: Discovered a compatibility issue with existing materialized view consumers that assume immutable object names. Agreed to publish lineage notifications and provide backward-compatible aliasing in object registry.
2026-03-09: Performance baseline run planned next week to validate rewrite throughput and production latency impact. SRE to provide IO throttling knobs in worker fleet.
comments: PM (Rafael Gomez) 2026-02-17: Please include UI wireframes for the operator flow; we want an easy 'review & approve' step before any irreversible deletion.

SRE (Maya Singh) 2026-02-25: Concerned about IO impact during large rewrites; recommend built-in global QPS budget and per-customer concurrency limits.
